document_check.note: Seifallahi M, Galvin JE, Ghoraani B. 'Curve Walking Reveals More Gait Impairments in Older Adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment than Straight Walking: A Kinect Camera-Based Study'. Journal of Alzheimer's Disease Reports 8 (2024) 423-435, DOI 10.3233/ADR-230149. The title matches the summaries.md header for Paper 1082. The sample is 55 older adults (30 HC, 25 MCI) recruited through the Iran Dementia and Alzheimer's Association, each doing three single-task trials on a straight 10 m path and on an oval 10 m path, recorded with a Kinect v2 camera. Table 2 (extract page 6, journal page 428) reproduces every number in the cited result exactly.

cited_result: Table 2 (p.6), 30 HC vs 25 MCI, same participants, three trials per path. Single-task straight 10 m walking: average velocity 50.13 +/- 27.92 vs 47.39 +/- 9.80 cm/s, p = 0.780 (step velocity mean p = 0.574, stride velocity mean p = 0.177, cadence p = 0.247). Curved (oval) 10 m walking: average velocity 45.90 +/- 8.89 vs 39.27 +/- 10.09 cm/s, p = 0.007 (step velocity mean p < 0.001, stride velocity mean p < 0.001, cadence p = 0.018).
tool_reason: The cited result compares gait markers measured on one occasion between diagnostic groups (MCI against healthy controls) under two walking conditions. That is a group comparison at one time point, not model performance or index-test accuracy against a reference standard, so the brief's row for the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist applies. Recruitment was by diagnostic group, which is case-control-type sampling, but the review applies this checklist to biomarker-in-MCI-versus-controls comparisons.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion clearly defined
domains.rationale: Exclusion criteria are listed explicitly. The inclusion side is only 'volunteers' from an association's clients or from notices. No age threshold is given, and no diagnostic criteria define entry to the MCI or HC group.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Participants were selected following a comprehensive analysis of volunteers who were clients of the Iran Dementia and Alzheimer’s Association (IDAA) or had responded to notices and announcements about the study. ... Exclusion criteria for this study included individuals who were diagnosed with moderate to severe depression, were taking medication that could interfere with testing, had undergone surgery such as knee or hip replacement, or had experienced a stroke. (Looked for: an age range for inclusion and named entry criteria for the MCI and HC groups; none found.)

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Group sizes, the recruitment source, the country and ethics body, and demographic and clinical characteristics by group (age, sex, BMI, education, MMSE, MoCA, GDS) are reported. Recruitment dates and the place where testing was done are not given.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: A total of 55 participants, comprising 30 HC individuals and 25 individuals with MCI, were recruited for the study. [p.2] ... Age (y) 68.33 ± 2.15 69.76 ± 6.45 0.091 ... BMI (kg/m2) 24.51 ± 2.67 26.67 ± 2.62 <0.001∗ ... Years of education 13.53 ± 3.05 11.56 ± 3.00 0.008∗ [Table 1, p.5]

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (diagnostic group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Group membership comes from a clinical evaluation by the IDAA, and the components are named and applied to both groups. The document does not say who made the diagnoses, give any inter-rater reliability, or say whether the diagnosis was made independently of the gait testing.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: The individuals with MCI were diagnosed by the IDAA based on a comprehensive evaluation, including brain imaging, electroencephalography (EEG), neuropsychological assessments, and physical examinations. The HC participants underwent a similar evaluation but were without any cognitive impairment. (Looked for: the diagnosing clinicians, a diagnostic protocol, reliability, and independence from the gait recording; none reported.)

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: No standard MCI criteria (for example Petersen, NIA-AA or DSM-5 mild neurocognitive disorder) and no MoCA or MMSE cut-offs are named. The authors acknowledge that the diagnoses had no biomarker verification. The group scores are clearly separated (MMSE 28.50 vs 25.60, MoCA 27.13 vs 22.76), but the classification rule is not stated.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: The Persian version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) were utilized to assess cognitive status. [p.2] ... While this study primarily emphasized MCI and HC participants and did not incorporate dual-task walking tests or biomarker verification for MCI diagnoses, it lays the foundational groundwork for expansive research in the domain. [p.11] (Looked for: named MCI diagnostic criteria or test cut-offs; none reported.)

domains.rationale: BMI, education and depression (GDS) are identified as confounders, and age and sex are checked for balance. The confounders were chosen by significance testing of baseline imbalance, and physical factors that affect gait (height or leg length, comorbidity, physical activity) are not considered. Confounders were nonetheless identified.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: ANCOVA (Analysis of Covariance) was used to adjust the extracted gait markers for the confounding variables of BMI, years of education, and GDS scores, which showed significant differences between the two groups [31]. [p.3] ... There were no significant differences in age and gender distribution between the two groups. However, the two groups had significant differences in body mass index (BMI), years of education, and GDS scores. [p.3]

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: An adjustment strategy (ANCOVA for BMI, education and GDS) is stated twice. The note beneath Table 2, which holds the cited result, says its values were adjusted for BMI only, so the covariate set behind the cited numbers is contradictory. It is also not said how adjustment was done for the non-normal markers tested with Mann-Whitney U, a test that cannot take covariates. Age was not adjusted: p = 0.091, with a much narrower HC distribution (SD 2.15 vs 6.45).

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: We extracted 50 gait markers from the recorded signals for each condition, controlling for confounding factors such as BMI, years of education, and GDS scores. [p.5] ... The values listed in Table 2 have been adjusted for BMI, in line with findings from Zhou et al. (2020) [32]. [p.6]

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes (gait markers) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Measurement is instrumented and automated, uses the same protocol for both groups, and averages three trials per path, which limits assessor bias. Validity is asserted by citation, not assessed in this study, and no test-retest reliability is reported. The oval's dimensions and the camera's position relative to the 10 m paths are not described. The HC straight-walking velocity SD (27.92 cm/s) is about four times the HC step- and stride-velocity SDs in the same condition (7.04 and 7.22), which points to an unaddressed outlier or tracking artefact in one of the null markers cited.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Each test covered a distance of 10 meters, a recognized standard for reliable gait assessment across populations, including MCI subjects [16–18]. For each participant, three trials were conducted on both straight and curved paths, with the mean of these trials calculated to ensure robust gait analysis. ... The curve walking test involved walking around an oval path, while the straight walking test was conducted on a straight path. ... This study emphasizes spatio-temporal gait markers using Kinect v.2 for better validity [19, 20]. [p.3] ... Velocity (cm/s) 50.13 ± 27.92 47.39 ± 9.80 0.780 [Table 2, p.6] (Looked for: oval path dimensions, camera placement and coverage of the 10 m paths, in-study reliability or validity data, and outlier handling; none reported.)

domains.rationale: Each two-group comparison uses a standard test chosen by a normality check. Several problems remain. The text does not say which test (t-test, Mann-Whitney or ANCOVA) produced each Table 2 p-value, or whether the p-values are adjusted. There are 100 comparisons (50 markers by two conditions) at an uncorrected p < 0.05. The straight-versus-curved dissociation is inferred from significant against non-significant p-values, with no group-by-condition interaction test reported for velocity. The 'cost' comparison reports 13 significant marker costs without listing them in the text. No power calculation supports the null straight-walking results with 30 and 25 participants. None of these problems amounts to a clearly inappropriate analysis of the group comparisons themselves.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: For normally distributed data, unpaired t-tests were used to compare the gait markers of the two groups, while for non-normally distributed data, Mann-Whitney U tests were used to compare the gait markers of the two groups [29, 30]. ... A p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant for all analyses (p-value <0.05). [p.3] ... The costs of 31 out of 50 gait markers (62%) were greater for MCI than HCs when the walking tests changed from SW to CW, and 13 marker costs showed significant differences between the two study groups. [p.8] (Looked for: multiplicity correction, a group-by-condition interaction test, the test behind each Table 2 p-value, and a sample-size calculation; none reported.)

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 2 and 5 Yes; items 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 Unclear; no item No).
overall_rationale: By the review's rule, none of the four key items (confounder identification, confounder strategy, valid outcome measurement, appropriate analysis) is No, so the risk is not high. It is not low for several reasons. MCI and HC status rest on an unnamed clinical evaluation with no standard criteria and no biomarker confirmation. The covariate set behind the cited Table 2 values is reported inconsistently (BMI, education and GDS in the Methods; BMI only in the table note). The Kinect gait measures have no in-study validity or reliability data, the path geometry and camera coverage are undescribed, and the HC straight-velocity SD is anomalous. The analysis runs 100 uncorrected comparisons and infers the straight-versus-curved dissociation without a formal interaction test.

applicability.rationale: A volunteer sample of clear-cut groups from an Iranian dementia association and public notices, recruited by diagnostic status rather than consecutively. MCI is clinically diagnosed without biomarker confirmation. The HC group is narrowly aged (68.33 +/- 2.15 years). Stroke, joint replacement and moderate-to-severe depression are excluded. Results may not transfer to unselected memory-clinic or community populations.
Single-task straight and oval 10 m walking recorded with a Kinect v2 camera in the same participants. This is directly the unloaded-versus-loaded walking contrast that VF-25 describes.
